factors.name: Variant variability / log entropy
factors.summary: The largest factor (28% of variance) combines the number of variants, heterogeneity and many normalized entropy measures (EPA normalized entropies, k-block ratios, knn, trace entropy), with the top-k variant coverage ratios and variant occurrence loading negatively (-0.79 to -0.94). It describes how strongly traces spread over many distinct, rarely repeated variants rather than concentrating on a few frequent ones. Several minimum and low-quantile trace length measures (trace_len_min 0.77, distinct_activities_min 0.77) also load, and many measures cross-load with Factors 2, 3 and 5.

factors.name: Log volume and trace length
factors.summary: Activity occurrence statistics (max, std, variance, mean 0.80-0.91), n_events, central trace length measures and the unnormalized EPA entropies load together, while event_density loads negatively (-0.68). This captures how many events the log contains, i.e. longer traces and more frequent activity occurrences, which drive raw (unnormalized) entropies and edit distances. Several trace length measures cross-load with Factors 1 and 3.

factors.name: Activity alphabet and trace length dispersion
factors.summary: The number of unique activities and the spread of distinct activities per trace load highly (0.92-0.96), together with trace length dispersion (geometric std, coefficient of variation, IQR, std) and advanced_trace_diversity; trace_len_entropy (-0.84), epa_normalized_variant_entropy (-0.80) and density_dfg (-0.68) load negatively. It combines a larger activity vocabulary with more heterogeneous trace lengths and a sparser DFG. The blend of vocabulary size and length dispersion is less clear-cut than for the first two factors.

factors.name: Uniform start and end points
factors.summary: Location statistics of start and end activity frequencies load very highly (0.81-0.97), as do n_cut_vertices_dfg and separability_ratio_dfg, while the numbers of unique start and end activities load negatively (about -0.80). Logs high on this factor have few start/end activities that each cover many traces, together with a DFG containing many cut vertices. This is a clear, coherent factor.

factors.name: DFG size and connectivity
factors.summary: DFG edge count, cyclomatic number, max node degree, connectivity coefficient and number_of_successions load moderately (0.58-0.65). All of them also cross-load at about 0.53-0.56 on Factor 1, so this factor captures only the part of DFG connectivity not shared with variability; n_edges_dfg and cyclomatic_number_dfg are also linearly dependent.

factors.name: Loops
factors.summary: All loop measures of the Repetitions group load together (0.61-0.88) and on little else. The factor captures how often and how large loops appear within traces; n_traces_with_repetition instead loads on Factor 2.

factors.name: Dominant start activity
factors.summary: Only start_activities_variance (0.68) and start_activities_max (0.60) are assigned, with start_activities_std also at 0.55; start_activities_variance cross-loads negatively on Factor 4. It seems to reflect an uneven distribution with one dominant start activity, but rests on very few measures and explains under 2% of variance.

factors.name: End activity spread
factors.summary: end_activities_std (0.80) and end_activities_variance (0.79) form a two-measure factor reflecting uneven frequencies of end activities. It is a weak, near-specific factor.

factors.name: Trace comparison 'structure'
factors.summary: Only structure (0.71) is assigned, with mean_variant_occurrence loading -0.68 as a cross-loading with Factor 1. The measure definition is limited to its group name (Trace comparison), so the meaning of this factor remains unclear.

factors.name: Activity frequency shape
factors.summary: Kurtosis (-0.70) and skewness (-0.61) of activity occurrence load negatively, so the factor rises with a less skewed, less peaked activity frequency distribution. It rests on two measures only.

factors.name: Weak trace length histogram factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned; only low-communality histogram bins load moderately (0.35-0.52). It is a weak residual factor and should not be interpreted.

factors.name: Trace length histogram bins 4 and 7
factors.summary: Two individual histogram bins load highly (0.87, 0.83). This is likely an artefact of the binning, not a substantive dimension.

factors.name: Weak sequentiality/similarity factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned; the highest loadings are moderate (sequentiality_ratio_dfg 0.48, similarity_rate_variants 0.39, average_affinity 0.37). The factor is too weak to name with any confidence.

factors.name: Extreme trace length histogram bins
factors.summary: The first and last histogram bins load highly (0.89, 0.75). This likely reflects the mass in the tails of the trace length histogram and is narrow.

factors.name: Trace length histogram shape
factors.summary: Skewness and kurtosis of the trace length histogram load at about 0.70, with secondary loadings near 0.5 on Factor 3. It captures the shape of the trace length distribution but rests on two measures.

factors.name: Rarest activity frequency
factors.summary: activities_min (0.52) and activities_q1 (0.44) load moderately. The factor seems to reflect how frequent the least common activities are, but it is weak.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett significant, KMO 0.93), and 16 varimax factors explain 89% of the variance. Four strong factors dominate: variant variability/entropy (28%), log volume and trace length (16%), activity alphabet and length dispersion (13%) and uniform start/end activities (11%). Factors 5 and 6 add DFG connectivity and loops, while factors 7-16 each explain under 2% and mostly rest on one or two measures or histogram bins, suggesting the factor count is generous. Numerous cross-loadings, especially between Factors 1, 2, 3 and 5, show that these dimensions are not cleanly separated.
caveats: The correlation matrix is singular (e.g. n_edges_dfg with cyclomatic_number_dfg, trace_len_q3 with trace_len_iqr), so results rely on clamped eigenvalues and pseudo-inverses.
Communalities at the bound for n_events, mean_variant_occurrence and average_edit_distance indicate a possible Heywood case.
Measure definitions give only group names, so interpretations rest on measure names and group descriptions.
Factors 7-16 are weak, several are carried by one or two measures, and Factors 11 and 13 have no assigned measures.
Several histogram bins, end_activities_max, average_affinity, sequentiality_ratio_dfg and cyclicity_dfg remain unassigned.
The factors describe shared variance in this set of 2112 logs and depend on the data, the varimax rotation and the chosen factor count.
